observations: Photo 0: one swivel office chair on a five star chrome base with castors, in a living room.
Photo 0: padded black fabric seat with two adjustable armrests on black and silver posts.
Photo 0: the black mesh backrest is reclined almost fully flat, with a padded headrest at its far end.
Photo 0: gas lift column and a tilt or height lever under the seat are visible.
Photo 0: the headrest pad carries dust and lint; the mesh shows no visible tear from this angle.
Photo 0: no brand name, label or model is readable anywhere on the chair.
Photo 0: no receipt, warranty card or packaging is shown.
Photo 0: the chair is never shown upright, so it is not shown that the backrest returns and locks upright.

identity.kind: reclining mesh office chair with headrest

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows an office chair with the backrest reclined almost flat.
One photo only, at a distance; the headrest shows dust and the seat, mesh edges and base are not shown up close.
Repair history cannot be shown in photos.
No clip of the recline, height adjustment, swivel or castors working.
No receipt or warranty card is in the photo.

risks.risk: The recline mechanism may be broken, so the backrest may not come back upright or lock (the seller calls it bent).
risks.proof: A clip of the backrest being raised from flat to upright, locking at a few angles, with someone sitting back against it.
risks.if_unproven: as with a faulty recline that does not lock upright

risks.risk: The gas lift may sink or not adjust height.
risks.proof: A clip of the lever raising and lowering the seat and the seat holding height with someone sitting on it.
risks.if_unproven: as with a failed gas lift

risks.risk: Mesh, seat fabric or armrest pads may be torn or worn where not shown.
risks.proof: Close photos of the mesh, seat cushion and both armrest pads with the chair upright.

risks.risk: Base or castors may be cracked or missing a wheel.
risks.proof: A photo of the base from below showing all five castors.

proof_requests: A clip of the backrest raised to upright and locked, then reclined, with someone seated.
A clip of the height lever raising and lowering the seat.
A photo of the chair upright from the front and side.
Close photos of the mesh, seat and armrest pads.
A photo of the receipt or warranty card, if it exists.
response.reason: This is clearly a reclining mesh office chair with headrest, identified by type, and can be priced at its worst case as worn with a faulty recline until a clip shows the mechanism working.
